Tosafot on Bava Batra 122b:12:1.hebrew: סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת הוא ואין הלכה כסתם - תימה: נהי נמי דלא חשיב סתם גמור, מ"מ אהני הא דחשיב כרבים, וחשיב רבי יוחנן כרבים לגבי רבים, ויכול להיות הלכה כמותו. דהא בריש מסכת ביצה (דף ב. ושם) אמרי' גבי שבת: סתם לן תנא כר"ש, דתנן: "מחתכין את הדלועין" כו'. אע"ג דסתם ואחר כך מחלוקת הוא, דפליג עליה רבי יהודה, דקתני: "רבי יהודה אומר: אם לא היתה נבלה מערב שבת — אסורה". אלמא דלכל הפחות חשיב ההוא כרבים לגבי יחיד. ושמא גרע טפי כשאין מחלוקת בסמוך, דאיכא למימר דהדר ביה רבי מן הסתם ממה שסתם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 122b:12:1.english: It is an anonymous [mishnah] and afterward a dispute, and the halakhah does not follow an anonymous [mishnah] - This is puzzling. Granted that it is not considered a complete anonymous statement, nevertheless it still helps, in that it is considered as "the many," and Rabbi Yochanan is considered as "many" relative to the many, so the halakhah could be like him. For at the beginning of tractate Beitzah (2a, and there) we say, regarding Shabbat: The Tanna taught us an anonymous [mishnah] in accord with Rabbi Shimon, as we learned: "One may cut up gourds," etc. This is so even though it is an anonymous [mishnah] and afterward a dispute, as Rabbi Yehuda disagrees with it, for it teaches: "Rabbi Yehuda says: If it was not an animal carcass from the eve of Shabbat, it is forbidden." Evidently, at the very least that [anonymous mishnah] is considered as the many relative to an individual. Perhaps it is weaker still when there is no dispute immediately following it, since one can say that Rebbi retracted from the anonymous statement, from what he stated anonymously.
